_about: Growing parameters for the crop calendar (src/lib/crop-calendar.ts), merged onto each crop as `grow` by src/lib/crops.ts. The recovered live values (temp, days, start, nurseryWeeks, water, chill, staple; client module 54475 `r`) are unchanged except where `fieldSources` says so. Round 2 of the regional-accuracy audit (14 Oct 2026) added the fields in `fieldNotes`; every value cites a key in `sources` through `fieldSources`.

fieldNotes.overwinter: The sowing may be made to stand through winter (the clock stops in months under the crop minimum and in days under ten hours of light) and finish in spring or summer. Only these crops are allowed dormancy; every other crop must finish before the first month under its minimum.
fieldNotes.overwinterMinC: The mean annual extreme minimum (°C, the hardiness-zone basis) the standing crop takes. RHS 'mild areas' crops are read as H4 (−10 °C) on the RHS hardiness scale.
fieldNotes.sowMinSoilC: Minimum soil temperature for germination (°C, from the °F table rounded), tested against the late-month mean, which tracks soil at sowing depth.
fieldNotes.winterMinC: Perennials: the mean annual extreme minimum (°C) the dormant plant takes, tested against the place's meanAnnualExtremeMinC. Named for the brief; it is the plant's zone-style tolerance, not a mean-night figure. Zone ratings are read at the floor of the USDA zone named (zone 2: −45 °C, zone 3: −40 °C), since the field is tested against a station's mean annual extreme minimum; a figure the source gives in degrees is used as given (haskap: no damage at −47 °C).
fieldNotes.coolestMonthMaxC: Perennials that need a cool season: the coldest month's mean may not exceed this (°C).
fieldNotes.coldestMonthMinC: Tropical perennials: the coldest month's mean must reach this (°C) for the plant to keep growing and set fruit.
fieldNotes.maxWarmestMonthC: Heat ceiling: the warmest month's mean may not exceed this (°C); where unset the crop's own maximum plus 3 °C applies.
fieldNotes.garlic.days: 150 days is the tropical cycle (Greenlife Kenya, 4–6 months); outside the tropics garlic follows the autumn-planting model in crop-calendar.ts and ignores days.
fieldNotes.stands: The crop is left standing in the garden after it is ready and lifted at leisure, through frost, until the ground freezes (its `frostNote` / `ready` say 'leave it'). The calendar's harvest bar runs from the first picking to the last month with unfrozen ground, not for one month only.
fieldNotes.harvestAfterFrost: The crop is not worth picking before it has been frosted (sprouts 'bland before the first frosts'; parsnip starchy and flat), so its harvest bar starts no earlier than the town's average first fall frost, whenever the plants are mature.
fieldNotes.sowing gate: Added with the 2 Nov 2026 Ottawa audit (code constants in src/lib/crop-calendar.ts, not per-crop fields): tender crops are not sown or planted out before the average last frost + 7 days (RHS; the crop records); other crops that do not overwinter not before the average last frost − 21 days (Just Food Ottawa: brassica transplants 'no more than 3 weeks before the last frost'; Seeds of Diversity: cold-tolerant crops 3–4 weeks before). The harvest bar can start no earlier than the earliest sowing day + `days`.
fieldNotes.plantMinSoilC: Transplants and slips: the day's mean temperature (°C, read between the monthly means; the soil at planting depth tracks it) they are set out at. Sweet potato 18: the crop record's 'once the soil holds above 18 °C' (UGA C1014 waits for 70 °F). Added after the 10 Nov 2026 audit, which found sweet potatoes set out from February at Jacksonville, March at Savannah and April at Atlanta on the last frost alone.
fieldNotes.bulbs: A bulb onion: bulbing is set off by day length, whatever the planting date, so the calendar plants it by day length (src/lib/crop-calendar.ts BULB_*). Added after the 10 Nov 2026 audit (onions planted to June and lifted in November in New York, Philadelphia, Washington and Baltimore).
fieldNotes.regimes: Perennials: the only climates (src/lib/regime ids) the crop is listed in, from the climate zones its source names. Added after the 10 Nov 2026 audit (globe artichokes said to do well in eight humid-subtropical and continental towns with no source).
fieldNotes.winterAnnualAboveC: Where frost does not frame the year (the regime's frostLed, from the station frost dates) and the warmest month averages over this (°C), the crop is grown as a winter annual, planted in autumn and cleared after the harvest, so it is not listed as a perennial. Strawberry: UF/IFAS grows it as an annual in Florida because the plants decline once the summer heats up; Florida's warmest months in this site's records run 27.8–28.3 °C.
fieldNotes.plantMinNightC: Transplants: the day's mean night (°C, read between the monthly means) they are set out at. Tomato 10: the crop record's 'once nights hold above 10 °C'. Added after the 10 Nov 2026 audit, which found tomatoes set out in March at Atlanta (UGA C943: April in middle Georgia, later further north).
fieldNotes.frostEndsSeason: The frost that damages the crop ends its season, so the calendar holds it to the frost dates wherever the typical coldest night reaches its damage point (frostLimits damageC), not only its kill point. Potato: the crop record's 'the tops are tender: −1 to −2 °C blackens the leaves … it just ends the season'. Added after the Day 3 audit (11 Nov 2026), which found potatoes offered for November planting at Houston and New Orleans (coldest nights −2.0 and −1.6 °C) against LSU's September and AgriLife's Oct 1.
fieldNotes.plantAtRains: Perennials whose record plants them only 'at the start of the rains' (mango: 'so they root in before the dry season'; moringa): set out in the first month of each wet run of the place's regime, at no time where the year has no rainy season, and by warmth alone where it rains all year. Added after the Day 3 audit (11 Nov 2026), which found mangoes 'plant out now' at Brownsville in November with no source (Texas A&M gives no planting month).
